rationale: Identity, hash, size, record-field, figure and scope checks all pass, and no verification stamp is smuggled (honest zero-claim package). Two major, non-corrupting defects: a mis-declared locator offset that the programmatic gate cannot see (F-01) and one report-named implementation module missing from the inventory (F-02). Both are cheap to fix inside 01, so the package is returned for changes rather than rejected.

findings.finding: [F-01] Declared offsets do not delimit the declared quote: the locator claims [0,43) but the quote is 9 characters and searches back at [0,9). The byte-exactness contract (G2 E4: text[start:end] == quote) is therefore violated by the only whole-document asset locator.

[F-02] The report names `tools/pulse/gen_pulse_figures.py` among the implementation artifacts, but no asset in the manifest covers it. The markdown yields 14 distinct artifact paths; 13 of them are covered by the manifest's entries (ast-5611-02 is record metadata with no path), and the remaining one is this module. 01's stated purpose is a complete inventory, so a silent omission is a completeness defect even though every registered entry is faithful.

[N-01] Figure assets are name/caption-addressed only: the report record exposes `name`+`caption` and no bytes, so no content hash can be pinned. Not a producer defect (the source has no payload) but it means figure identity downstream rests on filenames, unlike ast-5611-01 which is hash-pinned.

[N-02] The whole-document asset's quote is 9 characters, below the gate's E6 floor of 12 for a *trivial* quote. Acceptable here only because content_ref.sha256 pins the entire document; if the pattern were copied to a per-claim locator it would be refused by E6.
